purpose: Ledgerline PR2: the model pipeline and the evaluation. A person asks a business question in plain English; a model fills in a typed intent, plain Python validates it against the registry, the builder writes read-only SQL, and the answer comes back with the SQL shown. This PR adds the LangGraph pipeline, the /ask API and `ledgerline ask`, a way to stand in for the real model without an API key (export the requests, answer them with a stand-in model, import the answers, every report labelled simulated), and an evaluation that scores Ledgerline against a one-shot baseline (the model writes SQL directly) on the fieldservice gold set and 5 Spider databases.
mechanism:
1. ledgerline/pipeline/prompt.py builds the system prompt from the registry; its version is part of every recording and checkpoint key.
2. ledgerline/pipeline/graph.py is a LangGraph graph: interpret (one structured-output call that returns an Intent) -> validate (the plain-Python validator) -> one retry with the validator's errors when validation fails -> execute (read-only executor) -> present (a deterministic answer: rows, the SQL, or a plain refusal). With refuse_on_budget on, a budget stop becomes a refusal instead of an exception.
3. ledgerline/pipeline/service.py wires the graph to a schema's registry and engine, gives each API ask its own per-request budget, and writes exactly one ask_log row per ask (answered, refused or error), including asks stopped by the budget.
4. ledgerline/api.py exposes POST /ask (FastAPI); ledgerline/cli.py adds `ledgerline ask`, `ledgerline eval` and the simulation commands.
5. ledgerline/llm/gateway.py adds --mode export|import beside record|replay|live: export writes each model request that has no recording to evals/pending/; import reads answer files, validates each strictly against the expected schema, and stores it as a recording with provenance {simulated_by, standing_in_for}. ledgerline/llm/simulate.py holds that format. docs/rerecord.md describes the loop.
6. ledgerline/bench/ is the evaluation: items.py loads gold and Spider items; systems.py has the Ledgerline system and the one-shot baseline (single_select() refuses anything but one SELECT, and the executor's untrusted=True path makes the database driver refuse a second statement); run.py runs items with checkpoints keyed by schema, model, trial, system, item, prompt version, registry hash and a hash of the scored item; metrics.py computes coverage, execution accuracy, accuracy when attempted, false refusals, wrong-when-answered and refusal recall with Wilson intervals; report.py writes the Markdown and JSON reports and checks the floors in evals/floors.yaml against the default model; compare.py matches result sets; spider.py builds Spider registries and checks their committed hashes (evals/spider_registries.json); privacy.py checks reports for Spider categorical values using hashes (evals/spider_forbidden_values.json, regenerated by scripts/spider_forbidden_values.py).
7. evals/reports/sim-1.md and .json are the simulated results; evals/triage/*.yaml tag each miss; scripts/check_replay_report.py checks the replay eval reproduces the committed report (run by verify.sh).
8. Core changes: registry_init types SQLite DATE columns holding only numbers as numbers; the executor gains untrusted=True; the gold set is at revision 2 (fs-032 corrected, recorded in evals/gold/CHANGELOG.md and MANIFEST.json).
decisions:
- No API key: model answers are simulated by a stand-in model through export/import, and every report says so; the fieldservice floor is recorded as not met in v0.1 (simulated) rather than tuning the prompt to the gold set.
- LangGraph only orchestrates; validation, SQL building and execution stay plain, tested Python (ADR-002).
- One retry, carrying the validator's errors; no open-ended loops.
- The one-shot baseline runs model SQL, so it gets two guards: a friendly single-SELECT check and a driver-level one-statement guarantee.
- A budget stop on an API ask is a refusal with an audit row; in an eval run it still stops the run so it can resume from its checkpoint.
- Checkpoint keys include everything that changes a score, so a gold correction is re-scored.
- Rejected: falling back to a live call when a recording is missing; scoring the floor on whichever model sorts first.
readers: README.md -> people trying or evaluating the project (recruiters, developers who clone it); docs/rerecord.md -> people re-running the simulated eval or recording with a real key; docs/adr/ -> engineers who want the reasoning; evals/reports/*.md -> readers of the results; code comments and docstrings -> the next maintainer. Cristian's rule for all of them: every comment, description and doc line deliberate, plain short sentences, terms defined on first use, no jargon-heavy decision prose.
